why_trail.why: Handoff read in full: task (force_reap + _release_child_plans), protected intent (zero active leases after archive, but never steal a live lease), test mode (test-after allowed, negatives load-bearing), close criteria (5 numbered tests), allowed scope (spine_lifecycle.py + its test file only), specific exclusions (checklist_engine.py/mcp_spine_server.py/spine_rail.py untouched), constraints (fixtures under tmp_path only), map anchors (spine_rail's _reap_binding_entries/_binding_transaction docstrings read, checklist_engine's release()/parse_args read to confirm --force --reason shape), required evidence, wiring grep, authority, stop conditions -- all present. Read source directly: _binding_transaction (spine_rail.py:397-436) loads+reaps+mutates+persists-if-differs, confirming an identity mutate suffices. release() (checklist_engine.py:1133-1148): ownership check is 'session_id != sess.get(session_id) and not force' -- with force=True the check never fires regardless of what session_id is passed, but echoing the child's own id would let a FUTURE accidental drop of --force slip through as if genuinely owned -- this is the real danger the handoff's honest-non-owner rule guards against. parse_args confirms release takes --session-id (required), --force, --reason. journal entries record the passed --session-id verbatim (append_journal_entry), so an honest caller id matters for the audit trail, not just the ownership check. Pre-change baseline: 95 passed, tests/test_spine_lifecycle.py 1774 lines.

force_reap lands as a two-line library call into spine_rail._binding_transaction with an identity mutate (lambda reaped: reaped) -- the mutate is not a no-op because _binding_transaction persists the reaped map whenever it differs from what it loaded, so handing it straight back makes the load-time reap durable NOW. Added a module-level sys.path insert for hooks/ beside the module's existing self-directory insert, and a top-level 'import spine_rail' alongside the module's other sibling imports -- zero edits to spine_rail.py (git diff --stat empty). Two tests: an innocent test proving the fixture precondition (target reads released before the call, asserted via spine_rail.load_spine) and that spine_rail.load_binding no longer carries the entry immediately after -- and a paired violating/contrast test that an ACTIVE target's entry survives unchanged, proving the reap is conditional rather than a blanket wipe. 2 new tests green, 104 total (95 baseline + 2 + 7 from the next gate's ReleaseChildPlans work done in the same working session but not yet advanced).

_release_child_plans lands: loads the parent spine, builds a declared_children set from every task's child_checklist (resolved relative to work_dir, then .resolve()'d, kept only if is_relative_to(work_dir) -- property 3 applied even at declaration time), excludes the bound spine's own resolved path from the scan (mirroring close_work's spine/journal exclusion -- without it the parent's own active lease would falsely show up as unclaimed_active, since nothing declares itself as its own child), then walks every *.json under work_dir once: active-leased + declared -> release via _engine_call's single choke point with --session-id <parent's own engine_session.session_id> --force --reason <reason>, appended to released on exit 0 else to unclaimed_active as a fail-safe; active-leased + undeclared -> unclaimed_active; anything else skipped. The caller id is read from the PARENT spine dict passed in, never from any child's own data -- confirmed by grep of the diff (no occurrence of reading a child's session_id). 0/1/2-children happy-path tests plus a spy-based test proving the exact --session-id/--force/--reason argv crossing the _engine_call choke point (release is not in MUTATING_VERBS -- checklist_engine.py:70-74 -- so it writes no journal line; a spy on the choke point is the only way to observe which id was used, corrected from my m0 assumption that journaling covers it). 7 new tests green, 104 total; fenced-file diff empty.

The three NEGATIVE tests needed no production change beyond m2's implementation -- each reproduces the boundary directly: (1) test_violating_a_spine_outside_work_dir_sharing_a_prefix_is_never_touched -- a sibling directory 'cmdr-g2' beside work_dir 'cmdr-g' (string prefix match, path-containment mismatch) is never scanned at all, since resolved_work_dir.rglob is structurally scoped to work_dir; its active lease survives untouched and appears in neither list. (2) test_violating_unclaimed_active_json_is_left_alone_and_reported -- an active-leased JSON genuinely under work_dir that no task's child_checklist names is left with status active and IS named in unclaimed_active, proving lineage (not proximity) gates release. (3) test_violating_a_symlink_inside_work_dir_escaping_outside_is_refused -- a symlink lexically inside work_dir, even DECLARED as a child_checklist, whose .resolve() walks outside work_dir is excluded from declared_children at collection time (is_relative_to check) and would be skipped again at scan time if reached; the real external target's lease stays active and neither the symlink's nor the target's path appears in released. All three run individually by name (pytest -v) and the full ReleaseChildPlans class (7 tests) is green. 104/104 total, fenced-file diff still empty.

All verification commands run: full suite 104 passed (95 baseline + 2 ForceReap + 7 ReleaseChildPlans); fenced-file diff --stat empty for checklist_engine.py/mcp_spine_server.py/spine_rail.py; wiring grep shows force_reap/_release_child_plans referenced only in their own module (definitions + docstring prose) and in tests/test_spine_lifecycle.py (9 call sites) -- zero production callers, expected since g3's finish_work does not exist yet; checklist_engine.main appears exactly once in spine_lifecycle.py, inside _engine_call, confirming the single choke point still holds after this gate's additions. git check-ignore exits 1 for both changed files (tracked, not ignored). IMPLEMENTER_RESULT written in full to the handoff's delivery path with all required evidence pasted (three negative test bodies + passing output, force_reap immediacy test + output, full suite pre/post counts, fenced-diff output, session_id-read grep, git check-ignore results), assumptions, one out-of-scope observation (rglob follows directory symlinks, only the file-symlink case was in the close criteria), and workflow feedback naming the MUTATING_VERBS correction.
